authoredNote: The two columns this file is about (Size at 13, Guarded at 19) are read off the SOURCE and follow from the ruling — the anchor is the declaration's NAME node, and `opaque type ` is twelve characters wide — so the pins were written before the analyzer ran and then confirmed against it. The pre-fix columns each row must NOT be are stated in the `note` fields: they are what the positional walk returned, and they are what a regression returns.
rationale: M60 scala fold (2026-10-10), the second half of the two-ruling pass the java/groovy folds also carried. The contract is M59 (#825): the anchor of a declaration is the line — and the node — its NAME is written on. This lane implemented it as `first named child that is not annotation/modifier/comment`, which is exact for `class Foo` and wrong for a MODIFIER-PREFIXED declaration, because tree-sitter-scala models `opaque` and `inline` as their own named child NODES: `opaque type Size = Int` anchored the `Size` symbol on `opaque` (column 1) and `final opaque type Guarded` on the second token (column 7). MEASURED over the 18,965-file scala corpus, 600-file lexicographic sample, 50,425 declaration name-field nodes: 141 disagreements, 22 `type_definition` and 119 `parameter`, EVERY ONE of them a modifier node, and every one of them on the SAME LINE as the name — which is why no `contains`/`extends` row moved in the A/B (`script/m14/lanes/jvm-rulings-ab.mts`) and only the symbol RANGE did. The fix reads the grammar's own `childForFieldName("name")` first, the same answer java's fold reads; the positional walk stays as the fallback and now also skips the two modifier node types, so it can only ever move a pick OFF a modifier. LINE-only pins were already in place (`scala/declaration-lines-825`), so this fixture exists for the half nothing pinned: the COLUMN. It is the family's shape, not a scala inventiveness — kotlin's `declarationLineNode` reads `findNameNode` first and documents the same reason (`private data class SuspendedObject(` put the class on its parameter's line).

expectSymbols.comment: a SYMBOLIC declaration name: the grammar's name field is an operator_identifier, and the new helper admits it, so `def ++` keeps the same anchor rule as `def apply`

expectSymbolRanges.comment: pre-fix startColumn was 1 — the `opaque` keyword token, which is not the name `Size` (written at column 13 of that line)
pre-fix startColumn was 7 — the `opaque` token after `final`; the name is at 19

forbidRelationships.comment: a modifier is not the declaration: the anchor must never be the `opaque`/`inline` TOKEN. Stated as a relationship forbid rather than as a range row because the harness forbids relationship rows, not range fields — the range half is the expectSymbolRanges pin above, and this row is the same claim at the edge the range drives.

note: NO pre-fix RELATIONSHIP row is forbidden here, and that is measured rather than omitted: the pre-fold analyzer was run on this exact file (HEAD blob, 2026-10-11) and every `contains`/`references`/`exports` row it emitted carried the SAME line the folded analyzer emits — only the COLUMNS moved (Size 1 -> 13, Guarded 7 -> 19). A line-level forbid row would therefore have asserted something no behaviour ever produced. Where the defect IS line-level (annotation, comment, multi-line clause) the forbid rows live in scala/declaration-lines-825, which pins them.
